reviewed.why: Each kept test guards one answer or refusal of the only change endpoint; the restart-status foreign-host test is dropped because the same OWN_HOSTS check is already guarded for GET by test_server_leaks and for POST by test_close_refuses_a_foreign_host.

tests.source: app.json uses docks: docks reads dock.json by its contract (docks/docs/dock-json.md, f61fbe6) and asks `port home zulu-clock` for the port

reviewed.why: Docks is an outside dependency and these tests catch a dock.json that docks would misread without saying so: a wrong port, a server it does not see as its own, a bad health path, a missed restart or a dropped MISSIONS_CALL. The icon test is dropped because a broken icon shows up right away on the Dock.

tests.source: app.json uses port: server.py:home_port asks the ports repo's `port home presser` / `port home cmd-fs` on each call; a failed lookup must show as failing in /status (docs/code-map.md Data flow, Other apps' ports)

reviewed.why: Both tests guard what the clock does when the outside `port home` lookup fails and then recovers: no crash, and a /status that reports the real state, not a stale or false one.

tests.source: docs/code-map.md, Endpoints: OWN_HOSTS 403 and SERVED_FILES 404 for every route; GET /missions cut by trim_mission; GET /source/presser cut by trim_summary

reviewed.why: These tests guard the Host check, the served-file list and the field cuts the Endpoints section names; a silent break would leak mission members, plan links or reporter contacts. Dropped: the own-host test (other tests already get 200 on 127.0.0.1, and a refused localhost breaks the page where anyone would see it) and the no-cache test (it rests on a decisions.md entry, not an endpoint).
